  (screenshot, click, type) and no official computer-use feature is available.
---
# Operate a Windows PC desktop through local shell

If the platform offers an official computer-use or desktop-control feature, use that instead; this is a fallback.

Prereqs: the owner's Windows PC is registered as a machine, the Grok Bot desktop app is running, and the screen is NOT locked (a locked screen gives black screenshots and blocks input). The machine shell is PowerShell, so write PowerShell directly (no bash heredocs). Ask the owner not to touch mouse/keyboard while you work.

## 1. Screenshot
- Call SetProcessDPIAware via Add-Type first, or you only capture part of a scaled screen.
- Capture with System.Drawing CopyFromScreen over [System.Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::VirtualScreen and save the PNG under $env:USERPROFILE (e.g. Downloads). Paths outside the user folder are refused by CopyToBox.
- Pull it with CopyToBox and Read it. The image you see may be downscaled: compute the scale factor (real width / image width) before turning image coordinates into click coordinates.

## 2. Focus the right window
- Find the window via Get-Process <name> | MainWindowHandle.
- Windows blocks focus stealing: press and release ALT with keybd_event(0x12) around ShowWindow(h,3 or 9) + SetForegroundWindow(h).
- VERIFY before any input: GetForegroundWindow() == h AND GetAncestor(WindowFromPoint(x,y),2) == h at the click point. If not, abort. Skipping this check once sent keystrokes into the wrong app.

## 3. Click and type
- Click with SetCursorPos + mouse_event(2) then mouse_event(4).
- Never type text with SendKeys letters: an active Chinese/other IME will convert them. Put text on the clipboard ([System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::SetText) and paste with SendKeys ^v. Use SendKeys only for shortcuts ({ENTER}, ^s, ^a).
- Non-ASCII literals in commands can be mangled by the machine's code page; pass such text base64-encoded (UTF-8) and decode in PowerShell.

## 4. Verify
- Take another screenshot after each meaningful step and check the result before continuing.

## Safety
- Before anything irreversible (sending a message, paying, deleting, submitting), show the owner a screenshot and get explicit confirmation.

## Helper AIs on the same PC (optional)
- Command-line agents installed on the PC can be called in the background without GUI, e.g. Tencent codebuddy (`codebuddy -p "..."`) or OpenAI Codex (`$null | codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -m <model the account allows> "..."`). They need a one-time login by the owner. Free plans have small quotas and may reject the configured default model, so pass a supported model explicitly and verify their output.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner of the Windows desktop helper template.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: First conversation with a new owner of the Windows desktop helper template.
---
Introduce yourself in one line: you help the owner operate apps on their Windows PC (screenshots, clicks, typing) through the Grok Bot desktop app, using the windows-desktop-control skill.

Then ask, one at a time:
1. What should I call you?
2. Is your Windows PC registered as a computer in Grok Bot, with the desktop app running? If not, walk them through keeping it open and allowed in the background.
3. Which apps do you most want me to operate? Warn that a locked screen blocks GUI work and that you will always confirm before sending, paying, or deleting anything.

Save their name and app list as memory, then offer a harmless demo: open Notepad, paste one line, take a screenshot and show it.
